commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail

echo "== STEP 1: generate SSH CA key (if not present) =="
if [ ! -f /etc/ssh/ca ]; then
  sudo -n ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /etc/ssh/ca -N '' -C 'node1-ssh-host-ca' -q
fi
sudo -n chmod 600 /etc/ssh/ca
sudo -n chmod 644 /etc/ssh/ca.pub
echo "CA fingerprint:"; sudo -n ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ca.pub

echo "== STEP 2: sign the host's ed25519 public key with the CA =="
sudo -n ssh-keygen -s /etc/ssh/ca -I "node1-host-cert" -h \
  -n "node1,$NODE_NAME,$NODE_IP,localhost" \
  -V +52w \
  /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub

echo "== STEP 3: verify cert content =="
sudo -n ssh-keygen -Lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub

echo "== STEP 4: point sshd at the cert =="
CERT_LINE="HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub"
if ! sudo -n grep -qxF "$CERT_LINE" /etc/ssh/sshd_config; then
  printf '%s\n' "$CERT_LINE" | sudo -n tee -a /etc/ssh/sshd_config >/dev/null
fi
sudo -n chmod 644 /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub

echo "== STEP 5: validate sshd config and reload =="
sudo -n sshd -t
sudo -n systemctl reload sshd
systemctl is-active sshd

echo "== STEP 6: client-side test - trust only the CA, no host key pinning =="
mkdir -p /tmp/sshtest
echo "@cert-authority * $(sudo -n cat /etc/ssh/ca.pub)" > /tmp/sshtest/known_hosts
ssh -F /dev/null -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 \
    -o UserKnownHostsFile=/tmp/sshtest/known_hosts \
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes \
    -p 22 "$NODE_IP" -- true 2>&1 | tee /tmp/sshtest/connect.log || true

echo "== STEP 7: negative control - unknown key without CA trust should fail differently (sanity) =="
grep -i "certificate" /tmp/sshtest/connect.log || true
echo "DONE"
